title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
content_md: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments. In a FLASH advisory released Friday, the agency said multiple threat actors have weaponized the open-source framework since at least August 2026 to target organizations across the financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors. "ARTEX significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours," reads the FBI advisory. "The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale." ARTEX is an autonomous penetration testing framework written in Go that uses artificial intelligence agents to perform reconnaissance, discover vulnerabilities, exploit systems, escalate privileges, and steal data with little human intervention. Rather than using its own AI model, the framework integrates with external large language models (LLMs), including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, and Kimi.
